newsitem.title: FRANCE: France calls on Israel to restart peace process.
newsitem.headline: France calls on Israel to restart peace process.

text.p: France urged Israel on Thursday to restart the Arab-Israeli peace process "on the right footing" after Palestinian riots over the opening of an archeological tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem.

In a radio interview from New York, where he is attending the U.N. General Assembly, Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said he and European Union counterparts, as well as U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher, discussed the issue at a lunch on Wednesday.

"We agreed that we should express our common concern on the way events are developing on the ground and to ask the parties, and especially Israel, to take measures to ensure the peace process restarts on the right footing," De Charette told France-Inter radio.
"We all well understand that the Palestinians today are in a very difficult situation and it is up to us and to the Israelis especially to take the necessary measures," he said.
In Paris, the Foreign Ministry said the new troubles added to uncertainty surrounding the peace process.
"The restart of work on a tunnel...led, as could be expected, to demonstrations which were marked by violence," it said in a statement.

It said there a sense of "a return to the past" in the fact that the most serious incidents took place in Ramallah, Bethlehem and Gaza, a reference to the 1987-1993 Palestinian uprising, or intifada against Israel.

French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said after meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Paris on Wednesday that "there is no future in confrontation and violence, from whatever side, so discussions must resume". Juppe reiterated France's willingness to help get the peace talks back on track.
